block_05_direct_answer.title: Direct answer
block_05_direct_answer.body_html: Apartments and villas suit different budgets, lifestyles, maintenance needs and buyer goals. For townhouse buyers, compare usable space, privacy, location, service or maintenance costs, tenant or end-user demand, entry price and resale depth. The better property type is the one whose trade-offs match how the buyer plans to use or hold it.

items.answer: Apartments and villas suit different budgets, lifestyles, maintenance needs and buyer goals. For townhouse buyers, decide how the property will be lived in, rented or held before comparing apartment and villa characteristics.
items.question: Which is better: an apartment or a villa?

items.answer: A floor plan should be judged by usable space, not only total area. Compare bedroom widths, furniture placement, storage, kitchen arrangement and circulation against the way the unit is expected to be used.
items.question: What should I check in a floor plan?

items.answer: Unit size should be compared through usable space and layout efficiency, not area alone. Compare price against useful area and product quality rather than relying on total square footage without considering layout efficiency.
items.question: How should I compare unit sizes?

items.answer: A view premium is justified only when the view is durable and valued by future buyers. Consider service charges, maintenance exposure and other recurring costs that may accompany premium waterfront facilities or locations.
items.question: How should I assess whether a view premium is justified?

items.answer: A family area should make everyday routines easier, not simply offer more amenities. School or work travel would make the location inconvenient even if the property itself looks attractive. Shortlist areas against actual family priorities and then compare suitable projects within those locations side by side.
